title: Strict installation of a computed function
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet computing a function $f$ in time $T$. Then there exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $C$, two states of $C$ called entry and exit, and a natural number $a$, with at least one work tape, such that for every pair of Boolean words $x$ and $\mathrm{arg}$, the machine started on input $x$ in the entry state, with $\mathrm{arg}$ on tape $0$ and all other work tapes empty, reaches after some positive number $t$ of steps at most $a\bigl(T(|\mathrm{arg}|)+|\mathrm{arg}|+|f(\mathrm{arg})|+1\bigr)$ the configuration with state exit, $f(\mathrm{arg})$ on tape $0$, and all other work tapes empty. At every earlier time $u<t$, its state is different from exit.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$f$ is a function from Boolean words to Boolean words
$T$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
The machine $C$ has at least one work tape
There is a natural number $t$ bounded by $a(T(|\mathrm{arg}|)+|\mathrm{arg}|+|f(\mathrm{arg})|+1)$
The state is not exit at every time $u<t$
